hash_verification.live_code_after_review: Parent began V3 edits after the complete25-file verification; this report refers to the V2 manifest hashes, not subsequently changed live files.

decision: Strong improvement over V1 and a credible polished prototype. The major framing, brace-cadence, solid-jet and detached-cloud failures are resolved. Floor/shadow, aging vapor shape and fragmented deck paint keep the frozen stage below a source-grounded9/10.

excluded: known car-model V2 overlap/z-fighting issue and all car-model quality scoring
scope.source_comparison: Actual source frame19/20/22, wide17 and overhead37 were reopened. Source and implementation cameras/lighting differ; exact pixel alignment is not expected.
scope.full_path_end_note: A tiny car at the full-path end is a legitimate cost of showing the distant ramp and entire path, especially in portrait. It is not penalized as a clipping failure; the following view supplies readable action.

verified_improvements.result: Portrait release retains full ramp/car with margins. Wide mode retains ramp and complete path in both aspects. Previous wide clipping is resolved.
Arc-length spacing removes the curved comb and creates coherent bays without losing the recognizable profile.
Low flood banks, local white pools, red spill and darker floor replace the gray preview plane and prominent T-masts.
Opaque cyan blades/cones are gone. Thin noisy wisps better match the actual9.5s source phase. Preserve this gaseous direction.
The cloud now reaches and hides the car at landing. The car is clearly visible again at13s; preserve both behaviors.

remaining_findings.title: Visible finite floor boundary
remaining_findings.evidence: A hard brown-gray floor/black-background boundary remains around y550–585 in landscape-ready and y490–505 in landscape-end. Full-path end exposes a rectangular floor island; portrait-wide-end shows a horizontal floor band around y600–770 with black below. Source illumination falls naturally into darkness.
remaining_findings.action: Keep sufficient ground coverage, then fade final floor output—including diffuse, emission and received shadow—toward the background at distant/outer boundaries. Extending the box alone can move the same visible edge. Preserve local action pools and red spill.
remaining_findings.acceptance: Ready, following end and both full-path end aspects no longer reveal a bounded slab or abrupt horizon.

remaining_findings.title: Overly hard black shadows
remaining_findings.evidence: The crisp black C-shaped ramp shadow dominates ready/wide and overhead views, and the airborne car casts an isolated hard cutout. Source stage lighting has multiple broad sources and a softer, less graphic shadow response.
remaining_findings.action: Soften shadow filtering and tune bias, darkness and broad key/fill balance. Retain near-contact grounding while reducing distant pure-black cutouts. Avoid a broad sunlit-plane effect beneath isolated theatrical pools.
remaining_findings.acceptance: The ramp is grounded, but its shadow does not visually compete with its actual structure.

remaining_findings.title: Aging vapor remains a uniform dense loaf
remaining_findings.evidence: Landing placement/occlusion is improved, but landscape-landing has a long bright capsule of similar density from front burst to trailing mass. At clearance13s the car is correctly visible while the remaining right-hand cloud is a large smooth white wall. Source frame22/wide17 contain irregular coarse lobes, gaps, rising wisps and varied internal lighting.
remaining_findings.action: Preserve the dense local touchdown burst and visible car at13s. Reduce old-trail accumulated opacity/lifetime, vary coarse lobe height/size/density, and let aging particles become transparent and split into rising wisps rather than only grow. Add asymmetric gaps and subdued internal shading. Do not simply reduce all vapor globally.
remaining_findings.acceptance: Landing still hides the car convincingly, while clearance reveals a broken dissipating wake instead of a continuous white capsule.

remaining_findings.title: Fragmented ramp center stripe
remaining_findings.evidence: The overhead deck centerline appears as isolated flecks and short segments rather than continuous paint. Close ramp views also show a thin jagged line. This is separate from the excluded car overlap issue. Actual source ramp paint is coherent.
remaining_findings.action: Check stripe depth separation, segment joins and raster width. Use a continuous stable paint ribbon/decal or depth-safe strip with adequate screen coverage. Add restrained deck finish only after paint is clean. The exact depth-versus-aliasing cause is not established from stills.
remaining_findings.acceptance: The overhead stripe remains continuous across the deck without speckling; the wider ramp remains clean.

remaining_findings.title: Regular schematic stage pattern
remaining_findings.evidence: Similar cool pools and parallel red strips form a tidy runway pattern. Source wide views have less regular intensity/footprints, distant glare and dim white apron alignment markings. This is a fidelity refinement, not the V1 lighting failure.
remaining_findings.action: Slightly vary bank intensity/aim, add restrained source-visible white apron markings and tune cool/neutral/red balance. Avoid unrelated props or brighter global fill.
remaining_findings.acceptance: The stage retains clarity while carrying more event-specific ground and lighting cues.

jet_assessment.decision: Substantially improved; do not restore solid cones.
jet_assessment.evidence: Source frame19/main9.5095s has thin blue pressure wisps. The9.5s stage capture is reasonably consistent in form, although paler. Frame20 shows a stronger pressure-to-ground phase.
jet_assessment.limit: A10.0s capture would better verify the strong pressure-column phase; submitted9.5s jets are early and10.5s descent is heavily vapor-obscured. This is secondary to the confirmed floor/cloud/paint gaps.

framing_and_UI.decision: Framing is largely resolved; controls do not obscure the active car/ramp in these captures.
notes: Small full-path-end subjects are a coverage tradeoff, not a failure. Retain the separate following view.
The portrait trailing cloud can extend beyond the right edge while the active car region stays framed; this is not scored as lost action.
Duplicate XR entry and development chrome are presentation cleanup, not primary stage blockers.

next_pass_order: Fade floor output and soften shadows
Break up aging vapor while preserving landing occlusion and13s clearance
stopping_guidance: The frozen stage is a credible polished prototype. These remaining visible material/rendering gaps do not support9/10 approval. Car-model repair alone should not be counted as resolving them.
